hook.text: Why this approach? And what breaks under load?

hook-more.text: Backend interviews ask those follow-ups more than they used to, and this series is about answering them.

probe.text: The ground is data structures and algorithms, complexity in Big-O, and your language's fundamentals, usually in live coding. Backend roles add system and API design, SQL, caching and concurrency.
probe.spoken: The ground is data structures and algorithms, complexity in Big-O, and your language's fundamentals, usually in live coding. Backend roles add system and API design, sequel, caching and concurrency.

ai.text: What has changed is the coding round. Since 2025, it has split in two.

ai-allowed.text: Some rounds hand you an assistant and grade how you drive and check it.

ai-allowed-who.text: That can be an hour extending a multi-file project with the assistant built in, or a round that hands you unfamiliar code to read, debug and speed up.

ai-banned.text: Others ban assistants. Using one without permission can disqualify you, and some rounds are back in person.

ai-why.text: Underneath is one problem: an assistant can finish a take-home, and nobody sees how.

ai-survey.text: Karat, which sells interviewing services, asked four hundred engineering leaders in its 2026 survey, so read its figures as one vendor's.

ai-survey-data.text: Seventy-one percent said AI makes technical skills harder to assess. Sixty-two percent of organizations still banned it in technical interviews.

ai-moved.text: So the time has moved to live rounds where the interviewer watches you reason: extending a multi-file project, reading and debugging unfamiliar code, and design discussions with follow-ups.

ai-llm.text: And system design now takes in features that call a large language model, or LLM: streaming, retries, cost measured in tokens, and prompt injection.

ai-ask.text: Ask the recruiter, round by round, whether AI is allowed, and prepare for both. Algorithm practice still matters where it isn't.

series.text: This series argues decisions, not syntax.

series-parts.text: After this one, nine videos answer a hundred and twenty-five of the track's questions, each once: system design in two parts, then API design, databases, concurrency, designing objects, reading code, algorithms, and the AI-allowed round.

series-python.text: The Python fundamentals page is left out, because it's syntax. Its design questions are covered under concurrency: threads, processes, async and the global interpreter lock.

practice.text: Every topic page has concept checks, three add challenges that run in the browser, and a bank of a hundred and ten multiple-choice questions covers the whole track.

next.text: As take-homes faded, the round that grew was design. Next: approaching system design.
